content_sanskrit: अथोपकार्या निषधावनीपतिः निजामयासीद्वरणस्रजाञ्चितः । वसूनि वर्षन्सुबहूनि बन्दिनां विशिष्यभैमीगुणकीर्तनाकृताम् ॥

meaning_english: Then Nala, the lord of Nishadha, adorned with the wedding garland, went to his own royal tent, showering abundant riches upon the bards, especially those who were engaged in singing the praises of Damayanti's virtues.

content_sanskrit: तथा पथि त्यागमयं वितीर्णवान्यथातिभाराधिगमेन मागधैः । तृणीकृतं रत्ननिकाय मुच्चकैः चिकाय लोकश्चिरमुञ्छमुत्सुकः ॥

meaning_english: Nala distributed wealth so generously on his path that the eager populace, for a long time, gleaned the heaps of gems that had been discarded by the Magadhan kings as mere straw because they were too heavy to carry.

content_sanskrit: त्रपास्य न स्यात्सदसि स्त्रियान्वयात्कुतोऽतिरूपः सुखभाजनं जनः । अमूदृशी तत्कविबन्दिवर्णनैः अवाक्कृता राजकरञ्जिलोकवाक् ॥

meaning_english: He (Nala) would feel no shame in the assembly due to his association with a woman. However, the common talk among kings, which was of this nature: 'How can such an exceedingly handsome person be a vessel of happiness?', was silenced by the descriptions of his poets and bards.

content_sanskrit: अदोषतामेव सतां विवृण्वते द्विषां मृषादोषकणाधिरोपणाः । न जातु सत्ये सति दूषाणे भवेदलीकमाधातुमवद्यमुद्यमः ॥

meaning_english: The false imputations of minute faults by enemies only reveal the faultlessness of good people. Indeed, if a real fault existed, there would never be an effort to impute a contemptible, false one.

content_sanskrit: विदर्भराजोऽपि समं तनूजया प्रविश्य हृष्यन्नवरोधमात्मनः । शशंस देवीमनुजातसंशयां प्रतीच्छ जामातरमुत्सुके नलम् ॥

meaning_english: The rejoicing king of Vidarbha, entering his inner apartments with his daughter, spoke to the queen, who had grown doubtful: 'O eager one, accept Nala as your son-in-law.'

content_sanskrit: तनुत्विषा यस्य तृणं स मन्मथः कुलश्रिया यः पवितास्मदन्वयम् । जगत्त्रयीनायकमेलके वरं सुतां परं वेद विवेक्तुमीदृशम् ॥

meaning_english: 'Kamadeva is but a blade of grass compared to his bodily splendor, and he will purify our lineage with his family's glory. I know that only my daughter is capable of choosing such a groom in an assembly of the lords of the three worlds.'

content_sanskrit: सृजन्तु पाणिग्रहमङ्गलोचिता मृगीदृशः स्त्रीसमयस्पृशः क्रियाः । श्रृतिस्मृतीनां तु वयं विदध्महे विधीनिति स्माह च निर्ययौ च सः ॥

meaning_english: 'Let the deer-eyed women perform the activities suitable for the auspicious wedding, in accordance with their customs. We men, however, shall perform the rites prescribed by the scriptures.' Saying this, he (King Bhima) departed.

content_sanskrit: निरीय भूपेन निरीक्षितानना शशंस मौहूर्तिकसंसदंशकम् । गुणैररीणैरुदयास्तनिस्तुषां तदा स दातुं तनयां प्रचक्रमे ॥

meaning_english: As the king was leaving, the queen, whose face he watched, announced the decision of the astrologers. Then he (the king) began the process of giving away his daughter, who was endowed with complete virtues and flawless from birth.

content_sanskrit: अथावदद्दूतमुखः स नैषधं कुलं च बाला च ममानुकम्प्यताम् । स पल्लवत्वद्य मनोरथाङ्क्रुरश्चिरेण नस्त्वच्चरणोदकैरिति ॥

meaning_english: Then, King Bhima, through a messenger, said to Nala: 'May my family and my daughter be shown your compassion. May that long-cherished sprout of our desire blossom today, watered by the water from your feet.'

content_sanskrit: तथोत्थितं भीमवचःप्रतिध्वनिं निपीय दूतस्य स वक्त्रगह्वरात् । व्रजामि वन्दे चरणौ गुरोरिति ब्रुवन्प्रदाय प्रजिघाय तं बहु ॥

meaning_english: Nala, having absorbed the echo of Bhima's words that arose from the messenger's mouth, said, 'I am coming; I bow to the feet of the venerable one.' After rewarding the messenger generously, he sent him away.

content_sanskrit: निपीतदूतालपितस्ततो नलं विदर्भभर्तागमयांबभूव सः । निशावसाने श्रुतताम्रचूडवाग्यथा रथाङ्गस्तपनं धृतादरः ॥

meaning_english: Then, the lord of Vidarbha, having heard the messenger's speech, summoned Nala. This was like a respectful Chakravaka bird, upon hearing the cock's crow at the end of the night, eagerly awaiting the arrival of the sun.

content_sanskrit: क्वचित्तदालेपनदानपण्डिता कमप्यहंकारमगात्पुरस्कृता । अलम्भि तुङ्गासनसंनिवेशनादपूपनिर्माणविदग्धयादरः ॥

meaning_english: During the preparations, a woman skilled in applying unguents, being honored for her work, felt a certain pride. Elsewhere, a woman expert in making cakes was shown respect by being given a high seat.

content_sanskrit: मुखानि मुक्तामणितोरणोद्गतैर्मरीचिभिः पान्थविलासमाश्रितैः । पुरस्य तस्याखिलवेश्मनामपि प्रमोदहासच्छुरितानि रेजिरे ॥

meaning_english: The facades of all the houses in that city shone, touched by rays from the pearl and gem arches. These rays, adopting the charm of travelers, made the buildings appear as if they were sprinkled with the laughter of joy.

content_sanskrit: पथामनीयन्त तथाधिवासनान्मधुव्रतानामपि दत्तविभ्रमाः । वितानतामातपनिर्भयास्तदा पटच्छिदाकालिकपुष्पजाः स्रजः ॥

meaning_english: Then, garlands made from cloth-pieces resembling unseasonal flowers, fearless of the sun, were stretched over the roads to form canopies. Their fragrance was so authentic that it even deluded the bees.

content_sanskrit: विभूषणैः कञ्चुकिता बभुः प्रजा विचित्रचित्रैः स्नपितत्विषो गृहाः । बभूव तस्मिन्मणिकुट्टिमैः पुरे वपुः स्वमुर्व्याः परिवर्तितोपमम् ॥

meaning_english: The citizens, adorned with ornaments, shone as if wearing armor. The houses, decorated with various paintings, had their splendor enhanced. In that city, with its jeweled pavements, the very body of the earth seemed to have been transformed.

meaning_english: Then the festive music began: solid instruments (cymbals) sounded quickly and repeatedly; stringed instruments resounded continuously and intensely; wind instruments reached a high pitch; and percussion instruments sounded with immeasurable volume.

meaning_english: The sound of the lute was not drowned out by the flutes, nor the flutes by the songs, nor the songs by the cymbals, nor the cymbals by the Huhukka drum, nor it by the Dhakka drum, nor the Dhakka by the Mardala drums, nor even they by another Dhakka, creating a harmonious blend.

content_sanskrit: विचित्रवादित्रनिनादमूर्च्छितः सुदूरचारी जनतामुखारवः । ममौ न कर्णेषु दिगन्तदन्तिनां पयोधिपूरप्रतिनादमेदुरः ॥

meaning_english: The clamor from the people, amplified by various musical instruments, traveled far and was as dense as the roar of the ocean. This immense sound was so great that it could not be contained even in the vast ears of the elephants guarding the cosmic directions.

content_sanskrit: उदस्य कुम्भीरथ शातकुम्भजाः चतुष्कचारुत्विषि वेदिकोदरे । यथाकुलाचारमथावनीन्द्रजां पुरन्ध्रिवर्गः स्नपयांबभूव ताम् ॥

meaning_english: Then, a group of married women placed golden pitchers on a beautifully radiant quadrangle at the center of an altar. Following this, they bathed the princess, Damayanti, in accordance with their family customs.

meaning_english: The nearby mango trees, as if defeated by her pair of breasts and forced into the servitude of carrying water, bent their tops. With their drooping flowers as faces, they seemed to wither from the burden of shame.

meaning_english: Having just been bathed, Damayanti then shone brightly in a silk garment as white as the moon. In this state, she beautifully embodied the twilight that connects the two seasons of monsoon and autumn, establishing a kinship between them.

meaning_english: With her thick mass of hair dripping water, she surpassed the sky on a rainy day caused by bursting clouds. And when wiped with a silk towel, she, radiant like the moon, surpassed the sky made beautiful by the moon's glow.

meaning_english: Her tresses, scattering drops of pure water, shone brightly. They seemed to be emitting white pearls of fame, earned by conquering the chauri-like darkness, their friend.

meaning_english: Her hair, made exceedingly bright by being wiped with a very soft bathing towel, shone greatly. She herself shone intensely, like a golden statue whose brilliance is enhanced by being polished on a whetstone.

meaning_english: If gold were to learn fragrance from a slightly trembling golden Ketaki petal, only then could it bear comparison to the splendid beauty of her limbs, which are naturally fragrant and have a throbbing lustre.

meaning_english: After she was led to a pure dais, her friends, who were experts in all the arts, quickly and distinctly decorated each of her limbs, a skill they had perfected through long training.

meaning_english: Even without ornaments, she is the pinnacle of beauty. Yet, she was adorned by her expert friends and was seen to be even more beautiful. She does not shine more because of the ornament; rather, the ornament shines more because of her. Having established this principle, what scope is there for any clever debate?

This was because the tilaka, having come on her forehead, was surpassed by the natural beauty of her lips and eyes.

meaning_english: One of the friends, mistaking the thick smoke rising from the incense for Damayanti's mass of hair, repeatedly tried to tie it. Realizing her mistake from the smiles of the other friends, she finally, after some delay, tied the actual chauri-like hair of Damayanti.

content_sanskrit: बलस्य कृष्टेव हलेन भाति या कलिन्दकन्या घनभङ्गभङ्गुरा । तदार्पितैस्तां करुणस्य कुड्मलैः जहास तस्याः कुटिला कचच्छटा ॥

meaning_english: Damayanti's curly mass of hair, decorated with buds of the Karuna tree, seemed to laugh at the river Yamuna. The Yamuna, with its dark, wavy ripples, looks as if it were being dragged by the plough of Balarama, and Damayanti's hair surpassed it in its curly beauty.

content_sanskrit: धृतैतया हाटकपट्टिकालिके बभूव केशाम्बुदविद्युदेव सा । मुखेन्दुसंबन्धवशात्सुधाजुषः स्थिरत्वमूहे नियतं तदायुषः ॥

meaning_english: The golden fillet worn by her on her forehead shone like lightning in the cloud of her hair. The poet infers that because of its contact with her nectar-filled moon-like face, this lightning (the fillet), unlike natural lightning, certainly attained a long and stable life.

content_sanskrit: ललाटिकासीमनि चूर्णकुन्तला बभुः स्फुटं भीमनरेन्द्रजन्मनः । मनःशिलाचित्रकदीपसंभवा भ्रमीभृतः कज्जलधूमवल्लयः ॥

meaning_english: On the edge of the forehead ornament of Damayanti, daughter of King Bhima, her curly locks of hair clearly shone. They appeared like whirling wreaths of black smoke rising from the lamp that was her tilaka mark made of red arsenic.

content_sanskrit: अपाङ्गमालिङ्ग्य तदीयमुच्चकैरदीपि रेखा जनिताञ्जनेन या । अपाति सूत्रं तदिव द्वितीयया वयःश्रिया वर्धयितुं विलोचने ॥

meaning_english: The line of collyrium, extending long and embracing the outer corner of her eye, shone brightly. It seemed as if a second measuring line was cast by the beauty of her youth itself, in order to lengthen her eyes.

content_sanskrit: अनङ्गलीलाभिरपाङ्गधाविनः कनीनिकानीलमणेः पुनः पुनः । तमिस्रवंशप्रभवेन रश्मिना स्वपद्धतिः सा किमरञ्जि नाञ्जनैः ॥

meaning_english: The path of her glance, which repeatedly darted to the corners of her eyes due to the play of love, was already colored by the dark rays of the sapphire-like pupils. Was it the collyrium that colored it? No, its own natural darkness was sufficient.

content_sanskrit: असेविषातां सुषमां विदर्भजादृशाववाप्याञ्जनरेखयाऽन्वयम् । भुजद्वयज्याकिणपद्धतिस्पृशोः स्मरेण बाणीकृतयोः पयोजयोः ॥
padaccheda: असेविषाताम् । सुषमाम् । विदर्भ-जा । दृशौ । अवाप्य । अञ्जन । रेखया । अन्वयम् । भुज । द्वय । ज्या । किण । पद्धति । स्पृशोः । स्मरेण । बाणीकृतयोः । पयोजयोः

meaning_english: Having been joined with the line of collyrium, Damayanti's eyes attained the beauty of two lotuses. These lotuses were imagined as being made into arrows by Kama, arrows that could reach the line of calluses on Nala's arms, formed by the constant use of the bowstring.

content_sanskrit: तदक्षितत्कालतुलागसा नखं निखाय कृष्णस्य मृगस्य चक्षुषी । विधिर्यदुद्धर्तुमियेष तत्तयोरदूरवर्तिक्षतता स्म शंसति ॥

meaning_english: The slight redness near the black deer's eyes suggests that Brahma, the creator, once wished to pluck them out after digging his nail into them, as a punishment for the sin of daring to be a match for Damayanti's eyes.

content_sanskrit: विलोचनाभ्यामतिमात्रपीडिते वतंसनीलाम्बुरुहद्वयीं खलु । तयोः प्रतिद्वन्द्विधियाधिरोपयांबभूवतुर्भीमसुताश्रुती ततः ॥

meaning_english: Therefore, Damayanti's ears, as if acting with the intention of creating rivals for her eyes, placed a pair of blue lotuses as ear ornaments. These lotuses were already greatly tormented (i.e., faded) by the superior beauty of her eyes.

content_sanskrit: धृतं वतंसोत्पलयुग्ममेतया व्यराजदस्यां पतिते दृशाविव । मनोभुवान्ध्यं गमितस्य पश्यतः स्थिते लगित्वा रसिकस्य कस्यचित् ॥

meaning_english: The pair of lotus ear-ornaments worn by her shone as if they were the very eyes of some connoisseur. Struck blind with passion by Kama, his eyes had fallen upon her, attached themselves, and remained there.

content_sanskrit: विदर्भपुत्रीश्रवणावतंसिकामणीमहःकिंशुककार्मुकोदरे । उदीतनेत्रोत्पलबाणसंभृतिर्नलं परं लक्ष्यमवैक्षत स्मरः ॥

meaning_english: Kama, holding a collection of arrows made from her upraised lotus-like eyes, looked upon Nala as his sole target. His bow was the red lustre of the gem in Damayanti's ear-ornament, which itself resembled a Kimshuka flower.

content_sanskrit: अनाचरत्तथ्यमृषाविचारणां तदाननं कर्णलतायुगेन किम् । बबन्ध जित्वा मणिकुण्डले विधू द्विचन्द्रबुद्ध्या कथितावसूयकौ ॥

meaning_english: Did her face, without considering whether the accusation was true or false, conquer the two moons (her earrings), who were said to be envious, and bind them with her creeper-like ears, mistaking them for two actual moons?

content_sanskrit: अवादि भैमी परिधाप्य कुण्डले वयस्ययाभ्यामभितः समन्वयः । त्वदाननेन्दोः प्रियकामजन्मनि श्रयत्ययं दौरुधरीं धुरं ध्रुवम् ॥
padaccheda: अवादि । भैमी । परिधाप्य । कुण्डले । वयस्यया । आभ्याम् । अभितः । समन्वयः । तव । आनन-इन्दोः । प्रिय-काम-जन्मनि । श्रयति । अयम् । दौरुधरीम् । धुरम् । ध्रुवम्

meaning_english: A friend, having made Bhaimi wear two earrings, said to her: "This combination of the two earrings on both sides of your moon-like face certainly plays the role of the two pans of a balance in enhancing your beauty, which gives rise to love."

content_sanskrit: निवेशितं यावकरागदीप्तये लगत्तदीयाधरसीम्नि सिक्थकम् । रराज तत्रैव निवस्तुमुत्सुकं मधूनि निर्धूय सुधासधर्मणि ॥

meaning_english: A piece of beeswax, placed on the edge of her lip to enhance the brilliance of the red lac-dye, shone as if it were eager to reside right there on her nectar-like lip, having rejected all other nectars.

content_sanskrit: स्वरेण वीणेत्यविशेषणं पुरा स्फुरत्तदीया खलु कण्ठकन्दली । अवाप्य तन्त्रीरथ सप्त मुक्तिकासरानराजत्परिवादिनी स्फुटम् ॥

meaning_english: Previously, her shoot-like throat, by its very tone, was simply a 'Veena' without any specific qualifier. Then, having obtained seven pearl necklaces like strings, it clearly shone like a 'Parivadini', a specific seven-stringed Veena.

content_sanskrit: उपास्यमानाविव शिक्षितुं ततो मृदुत्वमप्रौढमृणालनालया । विरेजतुर्माङ्गलिकेन संगतौ भुजौ सुदत्या वलयेन कम्बुनः ॥

meaning_english: The two arms of the beautiful-toothed Damayanti, adorned with an auspicious bracelet made of conch-shell, shone as if they were being attended upon by a tender lotus-stalk in order to learn softness from it.

content_sanskrit: पदद्वयेऽस्या नवयावरञ्जना जनैस्तदानीमुदनीयतार्पिता । चिराय पद्मौ परिरभ्य जाग्रती निशीव विश्लिष्य नवा रविद्युतिः ॥

meaning_english: At that time, fresh lac-dye was applied to her pair of feet by her attendants. It appeared like the new morning sunlight which, after separating from the two lotuses it had embraced and stayed awake with throughout the night, had just arrived.

content_sanskrit: कृतापराधः सुतनोरनन्तरं विचिन्त्य कान्तेन समं समागमम् । स्फुटं सिषेवे कुसुमेषुपावकः स रागचिह्नश्चरणौ न यावकः ॥

meaning_english: Anticipating her subsequent union with her beloved, it was clearly the fire of Kamadeva, disguised as the red mark of passion, that served her feet, as if seeking forgiveness for a past offense—it was not merely lac-dye.

content_sanskrit: स्वयं तदङ्गेषु गतेषु चारुतां परस्परेणैव विभूषितेषु च । किमूचिरेऽलंकरणानि तानि तद्दृतैव तेषां करणं बभूव यत् ॥

meaning_english: Since her limbs were already beautiful by themselves and adorned by each other, what purpose did those ornaments serve? Indeed, the very fact of being worn by her was what made them ornaments.

content_sanskrit: क्रमाधिकामुत्तरमुत्तरं श्रियं पुपोष यां भूषणचुम्बनैरियम् । पुरः पुरस्तस्थुषि रामणीयके तया बबाधेऽवधिबुद्धिधोरणिः ॥

meaning_english: She nourished a beauty that successively increased with each 'kiss' of an ornament. As this loveliness stood ever advancing, it obstructed any possibility of conceiving a limit to her beauty.

content_sanskrit: मणीसनाभौ मुकुरस्य मण्डले बभौ निजास्यप्रतिबिम्बदर्शिनी । विधोरदूरं स्वमुखं विधाय सा निरूपयन्तीव विशेषमेतयोः ॥

meaning_english: She, seeing the reflection of her own face in the jewel-studded center of the mirror, shone as if she were placing her face near the moon (in the mirror) to ascertain the difference in beauty between the two.

content_sanskrit: जितस्तदास्येन कलानिधिर्दधे द्विचन्द्रधीसाक्षिकमायकायताम् । तथापि जिग्ये युगपत्सखीयुगप्रदर्शितादर्शबहूभविष्णुना ॥

meaning_english: The moon, conquered by her face, became crescent-shaped like a bow, with the perception of two moons (her face and itself) as a witness. Even so, it was conquered again by her face, which became manifold in the mirrors simultaneously held up by a pair of her friends.

content_sanskrit: किमालियुग्मार्पितदर्पणद्वये तदास्यमेकं बहु चान्यदम्बुजम् । हिमेषु निर्वाप्य निशासमाधिभिः तदीयसालोक्यमितं व्यलोक्यत ॥

meaning_english: Was it that in the pair of mirrors held by her two friends, her single face was seen, while on the other hand, many lotuses were seen to have attained similarity with her face after being submerged in dew and performing nightly meditations?

content_sanskrit: पलाशदामेतिमिलच्छिलीमुखैर्वृता विभूषामणिरश्मिकार्मुकैः । अलक्षि लक्षैर्धनुषामसौ तदा रतीशसर्वस्वतयाऽभिरक्षिता ॥

meaning_english: Then she, surrounded by the bows formed by the rays of her jeweled ornaments which attracted bees mistaking them for flower garlands, appeared as if protected by lakhs of bows, because she was the entire treasure of Kamadeva.

content_sanskrit: विशेषतीर्थैरिव जह्नुनन्दिनी गुणैरिवाजानिकरागभूमिता । जगाम भाग्यैरिव नीतिरुज्ज्वलैर्विभूषणैस्तत्सुषमा महार्धताम् ॥

meaning_english: Her beauty, enhanced by brilliant ornaments, attained great preciousness, just as the Ganga river is exalted by its holy sites, as natural affection is by virtues, and as statecraft is by good fortunes.

meaning_english: The wives of other kings, who had come for Bhima's great festival, bowed down to obtain Nala's fidelity for their own husbands. They placed the lac-dye from Damayanti's feet on their heads as an auspicious mark for their husbands' long lives, just like vermilion.

content_sanskrit: अमोघभावेन सनाभितां गताः प्रसन्नगीर्वाणवराक्षरस्रजाम् । ततः प्रणम्राधिजगाम सा ह्रिया गुरुर्गुरुब्रह्मपतिव्रताशिषाः ॥

meaning_english: Then she, the venerable one, bowing down with modesty, received the blessings of the elders, Brahmins, and chaste women. These blessings, due to their unfailing nature, were akin to the garlands of boon-words from pleased deities.

content_sanskrit: तथैव तत्कालमथानुजीविभिः प्रसाधनासञ्जनशिल्पपारगैः । निजस्य पाणिग्रहणक्षणोचिता कृता नलस्यापि विभोर्विभूषणा ॥
padaccheda: तथा । एव । तत्कालम् । अथ । अनुजीविभिः । प्रसाधन-आसञ्जन-शिल्प-पारगैः । निजस्य । पाणि-ग्रहण-क्षण-उचिता । कृता । नलस्य । अपि । विभोः । विभूषणा

meaning_english: Then, at that time, in the same manner, the adornment of the lord Nala was also performed by his attendants, who were experts in the art of decoration, making it suitable for the moment of his wedding.

content_sanskrit: नृपस्य तत्राधिकृताः पुनः पुनर्विचार्य तान्बन्धमवापिपन्कचान् । कलापलीलोपनिधिर्गरुत्त्यजः  स यैरपालापि कलापिसंपदः ॥

meaning_english: The appointed attendants, after much deliberation, styled the king's hair. By this hairdo, which held the secret beauty of a peacock's tail and surpassed Garuda's wings, the splendors of all peacocks were outshone.

content_sanskrit: पतत्त्रिणां द्राधिमशालिना धनुर्गुणेन संयोगजुषां मनोभुवः । कचेन तस्यार्जितमार्जनश्रिया समेत्य सौभाग्यमलम्भि कुङ्नलैः ॥

meaning_english: The earrings, upon coming into contact with his well-combed hair—which resembled the long bow-string of Kamadeva joined with his bird-arrows—attained a special beauty.

content_sanskrit: अनर्ध्यरत्नौघमयेन मण्डितो रराज राजा मुकुटेन मूर्धनि । वनीपकानां स हि कल्पभूरुहस्ततो विमुञ्चन्निव मञ्जुमञ्जरीम् ॥

content_sanskrit: नलस्य भाले मणिवीरपट्टिकानिभेन लग्नः परिधिर्विधोर्बभौ । तदा शशाङ्काधिकरूपतां गते तदानने मातुमशक्नुवन्निव ॥

content_sanskrit: बभूव भैम्याः खलु मानसौकसं जिघांसतो धैर्यभरं मनोभुवः । उपभ्रु तद्वर्तुलचित्ररूपिणी धनुःसमीपे गुलिकेव संभृता ॥

content_sanskrit: अचुम्बि या चन्दनबिन्दुमण्डली नलीयवक्त्रेण सरोजतर्जिना । श्रियं श्रिता काचन तारकासखी कृता शशाङ्कस्य तयाङ्कवर्तिनी ॥

Having attained great splendor from the kiss, it was made by that very pattern to reside within the mark of the moon (Damayanti's face).

content_sanskrit: न यावदग्निभ्रममेत्युदूढतां नलस्य भैमीति हरेर्दुराशया । स बिन्दुरिन्दुः प्रहितः किमस्य सा न वेति भाले पठितुं लिपीमिव ॥

meaning_english: Before Indra's wicked hope that Damayanti would not be married to Nala was dispelled, was that moon-like decorative dot sent by him? It seemed as if it were sent to read the script of fate on Nala's forehead to ascertain, 'Is she his or not?'

content_sanskrit: कपोलपालीजनिजानुबिम्बयोः समागमात्कुण्डलमण्डलद्वयी । नलस्य तत्कालमवाप चित्तभूः अथ स्फुरच्चक्रचतुष्कचारुताम् ॥

meaning_english: Then, as Damayanti sat on Nala's lap, the reflections of her knees appeared on his cheeks. Due to the union of these two reflections with his two earrings, the pair of earring-orbs acquired the beauty of a glittering set of four wheels, resembling the chariot of Kamadeva.

content_sanskrit: श्रितास्य कण्ठं गुरुविप्रवन्दनाद्विनम्रमोलेश्चिबुकाग्रचुम्बिनी । अवाप मुक्तावलिरास्यचन्द्रमः स्रवत्सुधातुन्दिलबिन्दुवृन्दताम् ॥

meaning_english: As Nala bowed his head to pay respects to elders and brahmins, his pearl necklace, resting on his neck, slid forward to touch the tip of his chin. In that moment, it appeared like a stream of plump nectar drops flowing from his moon-like face.

content_sanskrit: यतोऽजनि श्रीर्बलवान्बलं द्विषन्बभूव यस्याजिषु वारणेन सः । अपूपुरत्तान्कमलार्थिनो घनान्समुद्रभावं स बभार तद्भुजः ॥

meaning_english: Nala's arm bore the nature of the ocean for three reasons: from it, prosperity (Shri) was born; through its strength (and war elephant), the powerful enemy Bala was subdued in battles; and it satisfied the clouds which desire water (kamala). Thus, it resembled the ocean, the source of Shri, subduer of Bala, and filler of clouds.

content_sanskrit: रराज दोर्मण्डनमण्डलीजुषोः स वज्रमाणिक्यसितारुणत्विषोः । मिषेण वर्षन्दशदिङ्मुखोन्मुखौ यशःप्रतापाववनीजयार्जितौ ॥

meaning_english: Nala, seeing the clear reflection of his own form in the dense cluster of gems on his ornaments, which were worn to dispel heat, rendered useless the offering of a mirror by his attentive servants.

Having destroyed enemy kings in battle and possessing a victorious chariot, he resembled Arjuna, the son of Pritha, whose charioteer was Krishna, a descendant of Vrishni.

meaning_english: Then, the celestial women (Apsaras) of that heaven on earth, the city of Vidarbha, were overcome with eagerness to see the radiant Nala. Coming out from every house, fully adorned, they graced the royal roads, making them shine even more brightly.

content_sanskrit: अजानती कापि विलोकनोत्सुका समीरधूतार्धमपि स्तनांशुकम् । कुचेन तस्मै चलतेऽकरोत्पुरः पुराङ्गना मङ्गलकुम्भसंभृतिम् ॥

meaning_english: A certain city woman, extremely eager to see Nala, was so engrossed that she didn't notice the garment over her breast had been half blown aside by the wind. With her exposed breast, she unknowingly presented an auspicious welcome pitcher for the departing king.

content_sanskrit: सखीं नलं दर्शयमानयाङ्कतो जवादुदस्तस्य करस्य कङ्कणे । विषज्य हारैस्त्रुटितैरतर्कितैः कृतं कयापि क्षणलाजमोक्षणम् ॥

meaning_english: As a certain woman quickly raised her hand to point out Nala to her friend, her pearl necklaces unexpectedly broke. The pearls, getting caught on her bracelet, scattered, creating the auspicious, albeit accidental, ritual of showering fried grains for a moment.

content_sanskrit: लसन्नखादर्शमुखाम्बुजस्मितप्रसूनवाणीमधुपाणिपल्लवम् । यियासतस्तस्य नृपस्य जज्ञिरे प्रशस्तवस्तूनि तदेवयौवतम् ॥

meaning_english: For King Nala, who was about to depart, the group of young women itself became the collection of all auspicious objects needed for a journey. Their shining fingernails served as mirrors, their faces as lotuses, their smiles as flowers, their speech as honey, and their hands as tender sprouts.

content_sanskrit: करस्थताम्बूलजिघत्सुरेकिका विलोकनैकाग्रविलोचनोत्पला । मुखे निचिक्षेप मुखद्विराजतारुषेव लीलाकमलं विलासिनी ॥

meaning_english: A playful woman, her lotus-like eyes completely absorbed in watching Nala, intended to place the betel leaf from her hand into her mouth. Distracted, she instead put her play-lotus in her mouth, as if in anger at the presence of two moons (her own moon-like face and Nala's).

content_sanskrit: कयापि वीक्षाविमनस्कलोचने समाज एवोपपतेः समीयुषः । घनं सविघ्नं परिरम्भसाहसैः तदा तदालोकनमन्वभूयत ॥

meaning_english: At that moment, a certain woman's viewing of Nala was intensely and repeatedly obstructed. While her eyes were distracted by the sight of the king, her own lover, having approached her in the crowd, was making bold attempts to embrace her.

content_sanskrit: दिदृक्षुरन्या विनिमेषावीक्षणां नृणामयोग्यां दधती तनुश्रियम् । पदाग्रमात्रेण यदस्पृशन्महीं न तावता केवलमप्सरोऽभवत् ॥

meaning_english: Another woman, eager to see Nala, possessed an unblinking gaze and a bodily splendor not found in mortals. She had all the characteristics of a celestial nymph (Apsara); the only reason she was not one was the fact that she touched the earth, even if only with the very tips of her toes.

content_sanskrit: विभूषणस्रंसनशंसनार्पितैः करप्रहारैरपि धूननैरपि । अमान्तमन्तः प्रसभं पुराऽपरा सखीषु संमापयतीव संमदम् ॥

meaning_english: Another woman, whose immense joy could not be contained within herself, seemed to be forcibly transferring it to her friends. She did this through playful hand-slaps and shoves, under the pretext of alerting them to their slipping ornaments.

content_sanskrit: वतंसनीलाम्बुरुहेण किं दृशा विलोकमाने विमनीबभूवतुः । अपि श्रुती दर्शनसक्तचेतसां न तेन ते शुश्रुवतुर्मृगीदृशाम् ॥

meaning_english: The poet asks rhetorically: were the two seeing eyes of the women dejected by the blue lotus ear-ornament, viewing it as a rival for beauty? Furthermore, because the minds of these deer-eyed women were so completely captivated by the sight of Nala, their ears failed to hear anything at all.

content_sanskrit: काश्चिन्निर्माय चक्षुःप्रसृतिचुलुकितं तास्वशङ्कन्त कान्ता मौग्ध्यादाचूडमोघैर्निचुलितमिव तं भूषणानां मणीनाम् । साहस्रीभिर्निमेषाकृतमतिभिरयं दृग्भिरालिङ्गितः किं ज्योतिष्टोमादियज्ञश्रुतिफलजगतीसार्वभौमभ्रमेण ॥
padaccheda: काश्चित् । निर्माय । चक्षुःप्रसृतिचुलुकितम् । तासु । अशङ्कन्त । कान्ताः । मौग्ध्यात् । आचूडम् । ओघैः । निचुलितम् । इव । तम् । भूषणानाम् । मणीनाम् । साहस्रीभिः । निमेषाकृतमतिभिः । अयम् । दृग्भिः । आलिङ्गितः । किम् । ज्योतिष्टोमादियज्ञश्रुतिफलजगतीसार्वभौमभ्रमेण

Was he being embraced by thousands of unblinking eyes due to the illusion that he was the emperor of the world, the fruit of Vedic sacrifices like the Jyotishtoma?

content_sanskrit: भवन्सुद्युम्नः स्त्री नरपतिरभूद्यस्य जननी तमुर्वश्याः प्राणानपि विजयमानस्तनुरुचा । हरारब्धक्रोधेन्धनमदनसिंहासनमसावलंकर्मीणश्रीरुदभवदलंकर्तुमधुना ॥

meaning_english: This Nala, whose beauty is fit for adorning, has now arisen to adorn the throne of Kamadeva—which was fuel for the fire of Shiva's anger. He surpasses with his bodily splendor even Pururavas, the beloved of Urvashi, whose mother was King Sudyumna who had become a woman.

content_sanskrit: अर्थी सर्वसुपर्वणां पतिरसावेतस्य यूनः कृते पर्यत्याजि विदर्भराजसुतया युक्तं विशेषज्ञया । अस्मिन्नाम तया वृते सुमनसः सन्तोऽपि यन्निर्जरा जाता दुर्मनसो न सोढुमुचिता तेषां तु साऽनौचिती ॥
padaccheda: अर्थी । सर्वसुपर्वणाम् । पतिः । असौ । एतस्य । यूनः । कृते । पर्यत्याजि । विदर्भराजसुतया । युक्तम् । विशेषज्ञया । अस्मिन् । नाम । तया । वृते । सुमनसः । सन्तः । अपि । यत् । निर्जराः । जाताः । दुर्मनसः । न । सोढुम् । उचिता । तेषाम् । तु । सा । अनौचिती

meaning_english: That lord of all gods (Indra) was a supplicant. It was fitting that he was rejected for the sake of this youth by the discerning daughter of the Vidarbha king. But that the gods, though being 'good-hearted' (sumanas), became dejected when he was chosen by her—that impropriety of theirs is not fit to be tolerated.

content_sanskrit: अस्योत्कण्ठितकण्ठलोठिवरणस्रक्साक्षिभिर्दिग्भटैः स्वं वक्षः स्वयमस्फुटन्न किमदः शस्त्रादपि स्फोटितम् । व्यावृत्योपनतेन हा शतमखेनाद्य प्रसाद्या कथं भैम्यां व्यर्थमनोरथेन च शची साचीकृतास्याम्बुजा ॥
padaccheda: अस्य । उत्कण्ठितकण्ठलोठिवरणस्रक्साक्षिभिः । दिग्भटैः । स्वम् । वक्षः । स्वयम् । अस्फुटत् । न । किम् । अदः । शस्त्रात् । अपि । स्फोटितम् । व्यावृत्य । उपनतेन । हा । शतमखेन । अद्य । प्रसाद्या । कथम् । भैम्याम् । व्यर्थमनोरथेन । च । शची । साचीकृतास्याम्बुजा
anvaya: अस्य उत्कण्ठित-कण्ठ-लोठि-वरण-स्रक्-साक्षिभिः दिग्भटैः स्वम् वक्षः स्वयम् किम् न अस्फुटत्? अदः शस्त्रात् अपि स्फोटितम् । हा! भैम्याम् व्यर्थ-मनोरथेन व्यावृत्य उपनतेन शतमखेन अद्य साचीकृत-आस्य-अम्बुजा शची कथम् प्रसाद्या?
meaning_english: Why did the chests of the guardian deities, who witnessed the wedding garland rolling on Nala's eager neck, not burst on their own? That would have been more explosive than a weapon's strike. Alas! How can Indra, his desire for Damayanti thwarted, having turned back and approached Sachi, now propitiate her whose lotus-face is turned away in anger?

content_sanskrit: मा जानीत विदर्भजामविदुषीं कीर्तिं मुदः श्रोयसीं सेयं भद्रमचीकरन्मघवता न स्वां द्वितीयां शचीम् । कः शच्या रचयांचकार चरिते काव्यं स नः कथ्यतामेतस्यास्तु करिष्यते रसधुनीपात्रे चरित्रे न कैः ॥
padaccheda: मा । जानीत । विदर्भजाम् । अविदुषीम् । कीर्तिम् । मुदः । श्रेयसीम् । सा । इयम् । भद्रम् । अचीकरत् । मघवता । न । स्वाम् । द्वितीयाम् । शचीम् । कः । शच्याः । चरिते । काव्यम् । रचयांचकार । सः । नः । कथ्यताम् । एतस्याः । तु । करिष्यते । रसधुनीपात्रे । चरित्रे । न । कैः
anvaya: विदर्भजाम् मुदः कीर्तिम् श्रेयसीम् अविदुषीम् मा जानीत । सा इयम् मघवता स्वाम् द्वितीयाम् शचीम् न (कृत्वा) भद्रम् अचीकरत् । कः शच्याः चरिते काव्यम् रचयांचकार? सः नः कथ्यताम् । तु एतस्याः रस-धुनी-पात्रे चरिते कैः (काव्यम्) न करिष्यते?
meaning_english: Do not think Damayanti ignorant for not knowing that fame is better than pleasure. By not making herself a second Sachi for Indra, she did a good thing. Who has composed a poem on the life of Sachi? Let him be told to us. But on the life of this Damayanti, a vessel for the river of poetic sentiment, by whom will a poem not be composed?

content_sanskrit: वैदर्भीबहुजन्मनिर्मिततपःशिल्पेन देहश्रिया नेत्राभ्यां स्वदते युवायमवनीवासः प्रसूनायुधः । गीर्वाणालयसार्वभौमसुकृतप्राग्भारदुष्प्रापया योगं भीमजयानुभूय भजतामद्वैतमद्य त्विषाम् ॥
padaccheda: वैदर्भीबहुजन्मनिर्मिततपःशिल्पेन । देहश्रिया । नेत्राभ्याम् । स्वदते । युवा । अयम् । अवनीवासः । प्रसूनायुधः । गीर्वाणालयसार्वभौमसुकृतप्राग्भारदुष्प्रापया । योगम् । भीमजया । अनुभूय । भजताम् । अद्वैतम् । अद्य । त्विषाम्
anvaya: अयम् युवा अवनी-वासः प्रसूनायुधः वैदर्भी-बहु-जन्म-निर्मित-तपः-शिल्पेन देह-श्रिया नेत्राभ्याम् स्वदते । (अयम्) अद्य गीर्वाण-आलय-सार्वभौम-सुकृत-प्राग्भार-दुष्प्रापया भीमजया योगम् अनुभूय त्विषाम् अद्वैतम् भजताम् ।
meaning_english: This youth, an earth-dwelling Kamadeva, is pleasing to the eyes with his bodily beauty, which seems crafted by the art of Damayanti's austerities over many births. Today, having experienced union with Damayanti—who is unattainable even by the immense merit of Indra—let him attain a non-dual state of their combined splendors.

content_sanskrit: स्त्रीपुंसव्यतिषञ्जनं जनयतः पत्युः प्रजानामभूदभ्यासः परिपाकिमः किमनयोर्दाम्पत्यसंपत्तये । आसंसारपुरन्ध्रिपूरुषमिथःप्रेमार्पणक्रीडयाप्येतज्जम्पतिगाढरागरचना प्राकर्षि चेतोभुवः ॥
padaccheda: स्त्रीपुंसव्यतिषञ्जनम् । जनयतः । पत्युः । प्रजानाम् । अभूत् । अभ्यासः । परिपाकिमः । किम् । अनयोः । दाम्पत्यसंपत्तये । आसंसारपुरन्ध्रिपूरुषमिथःप्रेमार्पणक्रीडया । अपि । एतज्जम्पतिगाढरागरचना । प्राकर्षि । चेतोभुवः
anvaya: प्रजानाम् पत्युः स्त्री-पुंस-व्यतिषञ्जनम् जनयतः (ब्रह्मणः) अनयोः दाम्पत्य-संपत्तये किम् परिपाकिमः अभ्यासः अभूत्? चेतोभुवः आ-संसार-पुरन्ध्रि-पूरुष-मिथः-प्रेम-अर्पण-क्रीडया अपि एतत्-जम्पति-गाढ-राग-रचना प्राकर्षि ।
meaning_english: Was the creation of this couple's marital perfection the matured practice of Brahma, the lord of creatures who creates the union of man and woman? Or was the creation of this couple's deep love perfected by Kamadeva through his sport of inspiring mutual love between men and women since the beginning of the world?

content_sanskrit: ताभिर्दृश्यत एष यान्पथि महाज्यैष्ठीमहे मन्महे यदृग्भिः पुरुषोत्तमः परिचितः प्राग्मञ्चमञ्चन्कृतः । सा स्त्रीराट्पतयालुभिः शितिसितैः स्यादस्य दृक्चामरैः सस्ने माघमघातिघातियमुनागङ्गौघयोगे यया ॥
padaccheda: ताभिः । दृश्यते । एषः । यान् । पथि । महाज्यैष्ठीमहे । मन्महे । यदृग्भिः । पुरुषोत्तमः । परिचितः । प्राक् । मञ्चम् । अञ्चन् । कृतः । सा । स्त्रीराट् । पतयालुभिः । शितिसितैः । स्यात् । अस्य । दृक्चामरैः । सस्ने । माघमघातिघातियमुनागङ्गौघयोगे । यया
anvaya: एषः पथि यान् ताभिः (पौरस्त्रीभिः) दृश्यते । यत्-दृग्भिः पुरुषोत्तमः प्राक् परिचितः, (ताभिः) मञ्चम् अञ्चन् कृतः (अयम्) महा-ज्यैष्ठी-महे मन्महे । सा स्त्री-राट् यया माघ-मघ-अतिघाति-यमुना-गङ्गा-ओघ-योगे सस्ने, (तया) अस्य पतयालुभिः शिति-सितैः दृक्-चामरैः (सेवा) स्यात् ।
meaning_english: As Nala goes along the path, he is seen by the city women. We think it is the great festival of Jyeshtha, where he, like Lord Vishnu seen before, is made to ascend a platform by their eyes. That queen of women, Damayanti, by whom he was bathed in the sin-destroying confluence of Ganga and Yamuna (her glances), now serves him with her glancing black-and-white eyes that act like chowries.

content_sanskrit: वैदर्भीविपुलानुरागकलनात्सौभाग्यमत्राखिलक्षोणीचक्रशतक्रतौ निजगदे तद्बृत्तवृत्तक्रमैः । किंचास्माकनरेन्द्रभूसुभगतासंभूतये लग्नकं देवेन्द्रावरणप्रसादितशचीविश्राणिताशीर्वचः ॥
padaccheda: वैदर्भीविपुलानुरागकलनात् । सौभाग्यम् । अत्र । अखिलक्षोणीचक्रशतक्रतौ । निजगदे । तद्बृत्तवृत्तक्रमैः । किंचास्माकनरेन्द्रभूसुभगतासंभूतये । लग्नकम् । देवेन्द्रावरणप्रसादितशचीविश्राणिताशीर्वचः
anvaya: अत्र अखिल-क्षोणी-चक्र-शतक्रतौ (नले) वैदर्भी-विपुल-अनुराग-कलनात् सौभाग्यम् तत्-बृत्त-वृत्त-क्रमैः निजगदे । किम् च अस्माक-नरेन्द्र-भू-सुभगता-संभूतये देव-इन्द्र-आवरण-प्रसादित-शची-विश्राणित-आशीः-वचः लग्नकम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: The good fortune of this Nala, the Indra of the entire earth, was declared by the metrical compositions of that story (his marriage), arising from his winning Damayanti's great love. Moreover, the words of blessing bestowed by Sachi, who was pleased by Damayanti's rejection of Indra, served as the auspicious horoscope for the prosperity of our king's land.

content_sanskrit: आसुत्राममपासनान्मखभुजां भैम्यैव राजव्रजे तादर्थ्यागमनानुरोधपरया युक्तार्जि लज्जामृजा । आत्मानं त्रिदशप्रसादफलताम्पत्ये विधायानया ह्रीरोषापयशःकथानवसरः सृष्टं सुराणामपि ॥
padaccheda: आसुत्रामम् । अपासनात् । मखभुजाम् । भैम्या । एव । राजव्रजे । तादर्थ्यागमनानुरोधपरया । युक्तार्जि । लज्जामृजा । आत्मानम् । त्रिदशप्रसादफलताम् । पत्ये । विधाय । अनया । ह्रीरोषापयशःकथानवसरः । सृष्टम् । सुराणाम् । अपि
anvaya: राज-व्रजे आसुत्रामम् मखभुजाम् अपासनात् तादर्थ्य-आगमन-अनुरोध-परया भैम्या एव युक्त-अर्जि लज्जा-मृजा । अनया आत्मानम् पत्ये त्रिदश-प्रसाद-फलताम् विधाय सुराणाम् अपि ह्री-रोष-अपयशः-कथा-अनवसरः सृष्टम् ।
meaning_english: In the assembly of kings, Damayanti, who was mindful of the gods' request when they came as messengers, properly wiped away their shame from being rejected. By making herself the fruit of the gods' favor for her husband, she created a situation where there was no occasion for any talk of shame, anger, or disgrace for the gods.

content_sanskrit: इत्यालेपुरनुप्रतीकनिलयालंकारसारश्रियाहंकुर्वत्तनुरामणीयकममूरालोक्य पौरप्रियाः । सानन्दाः कुरुविन्दसुन्दरकरस्यानन्दनं स्यन्दनं तस्याध्यास्य यतः शतक्रतुहरित्क्रीडाद्रिमिन्दोरिव ॥
padaccheda: इति । आलेपुः । अनुप्रतीकनिलयालंकारसारश्रिया । अहंकुर्वत्तनुरामणीयकममूम् । आलोक्य । पौरप्रियाः । सानन्दाः । कुरुविन्दसुन्दरकरस्य । आनन्दनम् । स्यन्दनम् । तस्य । अध्यास्य । यतः । शतक्रतुहरित्क्रीडाद्रिम् । इन्दोः । इव
anvaya: पौर-प्रियाः अनुप्रतीक-निलय-अलंकार-सार-श्रिया अहंकुर्वत्-तनु-रामणीयकम् अमूम् आलोक्य इति आलेपुः । स-आनन्दाः (भूत्वा) तस्य कुरुविन्द-सुन्दर-करस्य आनन्दनम् स्यन्दनम् अध्यास्य यतः, इन्दोः शतक्रतु-हरित्-क्रीडा-अद्रिम् इव ।
meaning_english: Thus spoke the beloved women of the city, seeing Damayanti whose bodily loveliness was proud with the essential beauty of ornaments on every limb. They were joyful as Nala, whose taxes were as beautiful as rubies, ascended his delighting chariot and departed, like the moon ascending the Udayagiri mountain, Indra's pleasure-mountain in the east.

content_sanskrit: श्रीहर्षं कविराजराजिमुकुटालंकारहीरः सुतं श्रीहीरः सुषुवे जितेन्द्रियचयं मामल्लदेवी च यम् । यातः पञ्चदशः कृशेतररसस्वादाविहायं महाकाव्ये तस्य कृतौ नलीयचरिते सर्गो निसर्गोज्ज्वलः ॥
padaccheda: श्रीहर्षम् । कविराजराजिमुकुटालंकारहीरः । सुतम् । श्रीहीरः । सुषुवे । जितेन्द्रियचयम् । मामल्लदेवी । च । यम् । यातः । पञ्चदशः । कृशेतररसस्वादाविह । अयम् । महाकाव्ये । तस्य । कृतौ । नलीयचरिते । सर्गः । निसर्गोज्ज्वलः
anvaya: श्री-हीरः मामल्लदेवी च जित-इन्द्रिय-चयम् कवि-राज-राजि-मुकुट-अलंकार-हीरः यम् सुतम् श्री-हर्षम् सुषुवे, तस्य कृतौ नलीय-चरिते महा-काव्ये कृश-इतर-रस-स्वाद-अविह निसर्ग-उज्ज्वलः अयम् पञ्चदशः सर्गः यातः ।
meaning_english: This naturally brilliant fifteenth canto has concluded in this epic poem, the Naishadhiyacharitam, the work of that Sriharsha, who is full of rich poetic sentiments. He, the diamond ornamenting the crowns of the best poets and conqueror of his senses, was the son to whom Srihira and Mamalladevi gave birth.
